summary: The conference-speaker-management page is SessionBoard's end-to-end lifecycle page: unlike the sibling speaker-management page (portals, comms, progress tracking only), it chains the full conference pipeline — Speaker CRM sourcing, Call for Papers, Submission Evaluation, Manage Sessions and Agendas, Personalized Onboarding Portals, Dynamic Dashboards and Communication, and Content Management. Distinct deltas on this page: session assignment with overlap/room-conflict detection ("Assign sessions confidently"), document requests explicitly covering contracts and certificates of insurance, email AND SMS automation, batch content download by room/track/day, and the "submission to showtime" onboarding framing. Data flows without reentry: accepted CFP submissions become speaker+session records that feed the agenda and portals. Conference-specific findings: contracts are handled as document-collection requests (no e-signature claimed); travel is NOT a booking feature — Speaker CRM profiles store travel preferences, and SessionBoard positions logistics/registration as out of scope (handled by integrated platforms like Cvent/Bizzabo/Swoogo). Speaker records persist in a cross-event CRM with tagging, expertise search, session history, and prefilled reuse for returning speakers.
personas: Organizer/event content manager (admin): runs CFP-to-showtime pipeline, assigns sessions, requests documents, tracks status
Speaker/presenter: uses personalized branded portal to complete tasks, upload files, meet deadlines
Co-presenter/assistant/agency contact: limited-access collaborator on a speaker's sessions and deliverables
Reviewer/evaluator: scores submissions feeding speaker selection (owned by evaluation area; touchpoint only)
Attendee/public visitor: views published agenda with speaker, room, and time details

features.name: CFP-to-speaker lifecycle pipeline
features.description: Distinct to this page vs speaker-management: one connected pipeline from CFP submission through evaluation to speaker management and agenda. Accepting a submission creates/links speaker and session records automatically; 'information entered at the submission stage stays accurate and accessible throughout the entire event lifecycle' — no reentry or cross-checking.
features.ui_expectations: Accepting a submission produces a speaker record and linked session visible in the speakers/sessions area, carrying over title, abstract, bio without retyping.

features.name: Session and speaker assignment
features.description: 'Assign sessions confidently': assign speakers to sessions and sessions to rooms and time slots as part of agenda management (drag-and-drop implied by platform copy).
features.ui_expectations: Session detail view with editable speaker(s), room, date/time fields; assignments reflected in a schedule/agenda view.

features.name: Overlap and room conflict detection
features.description: Page contrasts with static tools where 'it's hard to see overlaps, gaps, or room issues until it's too late' — the system flags speaker double-bookings, schedule overlaps, and room clashes during assignment.
features.ui_expectations: Visible warning/flag (icon, banner, or highlight) when a speaker or room is double-booked in overlapping time slots.

features.name: Document requests incl. contracts and COI
features.description: Conference-specific delta: 'Send requests to collect certificates of insurance, contracts or any other types of documents' with deadlines, automated reminders, and per-request tracking. Collection-only; no e-signature claimed (inferred: signed docs uploaded as files, per category norms).
features.ui_expectations: Admin flow to create a named document request (type, assignee, deadline); request appears as pending task/row; uploaded file marks it complete and is tracked per speaker.

features.name: Speaker status dashboard
features.description: 'Track the status of every speaker with clear dashboards. Set reminders, send messages, and manage tasks from one place.' Speaker records carry status tags (Confirmed/Pending seen in UI captions); lists are filterable for bulk actions.
features.ui_expectations: Speaker list/grid with status chips, per-speaker deliverable completion indicators, filters (status, missing item), and bulk-select for actions.

features.name: Personalized onboarding portal (submission to showtime)
features.description: Overlaps speaker-management area; conference framing: 'Give each speaker a clear path from submission to showtime' — every speaker gets a personalized, branded portal with tasks, content, and deadlines 'so nothing slips through and everyone shows up prepared'.
features.ui_expectations: Per-speaker portal (unique link/login) showing event branding, task checklist with deadlines, file-upload areas, and the speaker's own session details.

features.name: Email and SMS automation
features.description: Delta vs sibling page: conference page cites email AND SMS automation for targeted outreach and reminders, with templates that auto-fill speaker/session details, sent and logged from one dashboard.
features.ui_expectations: Message composer reachable from speaker records with template picker and merge fields (name, session, deadline) resolving in preview; sent items logged per speaker. SMS channel optional/polish.

features.name: Batch content download by room/track/day
features.description: Conference day-of delta: files (decks, bios, videos) organized by session or speaker with batch download/export filtered by room, track, or day — for handoff to AV/production teams.
features.ui_expectations: Content library grouped by session/speaker with filters for room/track/day and a bulk download/export control producing an archive.

features.name: Cross-event Speaker CRM and reuse
features.description: Persistent speaker database across events: dynamic tagging, advanced search by expertise/topic, session history, ratings, communication logs; returning speakers' bio/headshot/history prefill new events; dynamic lists auto-update on criteria; smart import with auto-mapping.
features.ui_expectations: CRM area outside any single event with searchable/taggable profiles showing multi-event history; 'add to event' flow that prefills profile data.

features.name: Travel preference profile fields
features.description: Travel is not booked in-app — SessionBoard positions logistics/registration as out of scope, integrating with Cvent/Bizzabo/Swoogo instead. Speaker CRM profiles store travel preferences as data fields for coordination (custom fields norm inferred).
features.ui_expectations: Speaker profile includes editable travel-preference or custom logistics fields that persist after save; no flight/hotel booking UI expected.

features.name: Co-presenter and assistant access
features.description: 'Add co-presenters, assistants, or agency contacts with controlled access. Everyone sees what they need and nothing else' — scoped collaborator roles on a speaker's sessions/deliverables.
features.ui_expectations: Add-collaborator control on speaker or session records with role/permission choice; collaborator appears listed on the record.

features.name: Live agenda publish and embeds
features.description: Real-time agenda publishing to event websites via embeds; speaker names, rooms, times auto-sync when assignments change (primary ownership in agenda/content areas; listed here as the pipeline's visible output).
features.ui_expectations: Public agenda page/embed reflecting current session assignments; edits to room/time propagate without republishing manually.

rubric.criterion: Accepting a CFP submission automatically creates linked speaker and session records with submitted data carried over (no reentry)
auto_steps: Log in as organizer
Open submissions/CFP area and locate a pending submission (create one via public form if none seeded)
Accept/approve it
Navigate to speakers list and open the new speaker record
Confirm bio/name carried over and a linked session with the submitted title exists
rubric.pass_criteria: Speaker record and linked session exist immediately after acceptance, populated with the submission's name, bio, and session title without manual retyping
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of accepted submission, then screenshot of speaker record showing linked session and carried-over fields

rubric.criterion: Organizer can assign a speaker to a session and set the session's room and time slot
auto_steps: Open a session's detail/edit view
Add or change the assigned speaker
Set room and date/time
Save and reopen the session
Check the agenda/schedule view reflects the assignment
rubric.pass_criteria: Saved session persists speaker, room, and time; agenda view shows the session in the chosen room/slot with the speaker's name
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of session detail with speaker/room/time set, and screenshot of agenda view showing it

rubric.criterion: Double-booking a speaker or room in overlapping time slots produces a visible conflict warning
auto_steps: Assign speaker X to session A at Day 1 10:00-11:00 in Room 1
Assign speaker X to session B at Day 1 10:30-11:30 (any room), or assign session B to Room 1 same slot
Observe the UI during/after the second assignment
Capture any warning icon, banner, highlight, or blocking dialog
rubric.pass_criteria: A conflict indicator (warning, flag, or block) appears identifying the overlap; silent acceptance with no indication anywhere fails
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the overlapping assignments with the conflict indicator visible

rubric.criterion: Organizer can create a document request (e.g. contract or certificate of insurance) with a deadline assigned to a speaker, tracked as pending
auto_steps: Open document/file requests or tasks area
Create request named 'Signed speaking agreement' with a document type, assignee speaker, and deadline
Save and locate the request in a tracking list
Verify it shows the speaker, deadline, and a pending/incomplete state
rubric.pass_criteria: Request persists with assignee and deadline and displays pending status; email notification to the speaker is NOT verified by the agent
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of created request in the tracking list showing assignee, deadline, pending status

rubric.criterion: A file uploaded against a document request marks it complete in organizer tracking
auto_steps: As the speaker (portal link or seeded speaker login), open the pending 'Signed speaking agreement' task
Upload a PDF fixture
Switch to the organizer view
Verify the request now shows completed/received with the file attached
rubric.pass_criteria: Organizer tracking flips from pending to complete and the uploaded file is accessible from the speaker's record
rubric.evidence: Before/after screenshots of the request row, plus the file listed on the speaker record

rubric.criterion: Speakers carry an editable status (e.g. Invited/Pending/Confirmed) and the list is filterable by it
auto_steps: Open the speakers dashboard/list
Change one speaker's status to Confirmed
Apply a status filter for Confirmed
Verify only matching speakers remain; clear filter and verify full list returns
rubric.pass_criteria: Status edit persists after reload and the filter correctly narrows the list
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of speaker with updated status chip and screenshot of filtered list

rubric.criterion: Dashboard shows per-speaker deliverable completion so organizer can see who is missing what without opening each record
auto_steps: Seed or use speakers with mixed task completion
Open the speakers dashboard
Verify each row exposes completion state (progress count, badges, or missing-item indicator)
If available, filter/sort by incomplete deliverables
rubric.pass_criteria: Completion status is visible at list level and distinguishes complete vs incomplete speakers accurately
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of dashboard showing differing completion indicators across at least 3 speakers

rubric.criterion: Each speaker gets a personalized portal showing their own tasks with deadlines and their session details
auto_steps: Obtain a speaker portal link (organizer 'view as'/preview, or seeded speaker credentials)
Open the portal
Verify it shows that speaker's name, a task checklist with due dates, upload areas, and their assigned session
Verify another speaker's tasks are not visible
rubric.pass_criteria: Portal is speaker-specific (own tasks/session only) and lists actionable tasks with deadlines
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the portal showing speaker identity, task list with deadlines, session info

rubric.criterion: Speaker can update their own bio/profile in the portal and the change reflects in the organizer's record
auto_steps: In the speaker portal, edit the bio field to a distinctive string
Save
As organizer, open that speaker's record
Verify the distinctive string appears
rubric.pass_criteria: Speaker-side edit persists and is visible organizer-side without manual sync
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of portal edit saved and screenshot of organizer record showing the same text

rubric.criterion: Organizer can send a templated message to selected speakers with merge fields (name/session/deadline) auto-filled
auto_steps: From the speaker list, select one or more speakers
Open the message/compose tool
Pick a template containing merge fields
Verify the preview resolves fields to the actual speaker name/session
Send, then check the speaker record's communication log for the sent entry
rubric.pass_criteria: Preview shows resolved merge values and a sent-log entry appears on the record; actual email/SMS delivery to an inbox is NOT verified by the agent
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of resolved template preview and screenshot of the logged sent message

rubric.criterion: Automated reminders fire for approaching/overdue task deadlines
rubric.pass_criteria: Human: configure a reminder rule (or default) on a task assigned to a speaker whose email you control; set deadline within the reminder window (or in the past); confirm a reminder email (or SMS if claimed) arrives at that address referencing the task and deadline within the expected schedule
rubric.evidence: Copy of the received reminder email/SMS with timestamp, alongside screenshot of the reminder configuration

rubric.criterion: Speaker/session files can be batch-downloaded filtered by room, track, or day
rubric.pass_criteria: Human: seed files across at least 2 rooms/tracks/days; use the export/bulk-download control with a room (or track/day) filter; open the downloaded archive and confirm it contains exactly the files for the filtered subset, organized identifiably (folders or filenames by session/speaker)
rubric.evidence: The downloaded archive's file listing plus screenshot of the filter/export UI used

rubric.criterion: A cross-event speaker database exists with search/tag filtering and per-speaker history (past sessions/events)
auto_steps: Navigate to the CRM/speaker database area outside a single event
Search or filter by a tag/expertise term
Open a returning speaker's profile
Verify it shows history spanning more than one event (past sessions, ratings, or participation)
rubric.pass_criteria: Search narrows correctly and profile displays multi-event history fields
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of filtered CRM list and screenshot of profile history section

rubric.criterion: Adding a returning speaker to a new event prefills their bio and headshot from the CRM
auto_steps: From the CRM or new event's speaker area, add an existing speaker to a second event
Open the resulting event-level speaker record
Verify bio text and headshot are already populated, matching the CRM profile
rubric.pass_criteria: No blank profile: bio and headshot carry over automatically on add
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of CRM profile and screenshot of new event's speaker record showing identical prefilled data

rubric.criterion: Speaker profile supports travel-preference or custom logistics fields that persist (no booking UI required)
auto_steps: Open a speaker profile in edit mode
Locate a travel-preferences field or add/populate a custom field (e.g. 'Arrival: Aug 12, aisle seat')
Save, reload, and verify the value persists and displays on the profile
rubric.pass_criteria: Logistics data can be stored on the speaker record and survives reload; absence of flight/hotel booking is acceptable and expected
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of saved profile showing the travel/custom field value

rubric.criterion: A co-presenter or assistant can be added to a speaker/session with scoped access
auto_steps: Open a session or speaker record
Use the add co-presenter/collaborator control with a new email and role
Verify the collaborator appears listed on the record with their role
rubric.pass_criteria: Collaborator persists on the record with role shown; what the collaborator can actually see/edit requires a second account and is NOT verified by the agent
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the record listing the added collaborator and role

sample_data: Event: "TechSummit 2026", Aug 12-14 2026, 3 tracks (AI, DevTools, Leadership), rooms Ballroom A, Room 201, Room 202. Speakers (8): Maya Chen (Confirmed, 5/5 tasks, returning — 2 prior events, rating 4.6, tag: AI, travel pref "arrives Aug 11, aisle seat"), Diego Ruiz (Confirmed, 3/5, missing contract + slides), Priya Nair (Pending, 1/5), Sam Okafor (Invited, 0/5), Lena Vogel (Confirmed, co-presenter: assistant jordan@agency.example), plus 3 filler speakers with mixed statuses. Sessions (6) with title/abstract/track/room/slot; include deliberate conflict fixture: Maya double-booked Day 1 10:00-10:45 Ballroom A and 10:30-11:15 Room 201. Document request types: Signed speaking agreement (contract PDF), Certificate of insurance, Headshot (JPG), Bio (150 words), Slide deck (PPTX); deadlines spread Jul 15-Aug 5 2026 so some are overdue. Fixture files: contract.pdf, coi.pdf, headshot.jpg, deck.pptx. Email templates: "Speaker confirmation", "Deliverable reminder" with merge fields {first_name}, {session_title}, {deadline}. One pending CFP submission ("Scaling LLM Evals", submitter Alex Kim) ready to accept for pipeline test CSM-01.
gaps: Marketing copy only — no product docs/screenshots were directly inspectable, so exact UI layouts, field names, and navigation are unknown. Travel/lodging: no booking or itinerary features exist; only "travel preferences" appears as a CRM profile field, and SessionBoard explicitly scopes out logistics/registration (integrations handle it) — CSM-15 therefore tests data fields, not booking. Contracts: only document collection is stated; e-signature, contract templates, and fee/honorarium tracking are not claimed (inferred as out of scope). SMS automation is named but undetailed (provider, opt-in unknown). Day-of coordination beyond batch export ("showtime" framing) is implied, not specified. Speaker confirmation/decline flow (accept-invitation button) is inferred from status tags plus category norms (Sessionize-style). Conflict detection granularity (warn vs block) unspecified — rubric accepts either. Reviewer/evaluation and agenda drag-and-drop details left to their assigned areas to avoid duplication.
